propositions: A 0-byte enrich-drain.lock with no owner stamp leaks permanently when a drain process dies between lock creation and release, wedging all subsequent enrichment with no visible signal.
The current lock acquisition creates an O_EXCL file but never writes an owner stamp, leaving no staleness or liveness proof; collision always returns None without checking age or holder viability.

An extracted shared _stamp_is_stale core decision table allows drain locks to treat unrecognised (unstamped) stamps as reclaimable via wall-clock ceiling, while preserving mkdir lock's legacy stamp routing.
Bounded stale-lock reclaim on FileExistsError attempts create once more after reclaiming a stale holder, logging WARNING with holder description and age, then skips if a second collision occurs.
drain() skip log moves from INFO to WARNING and names the stamped holder so a wedged drain is visible without running doctor.
doctor_locks.py decodes the drain lock's v2 stamp and reports real staleness verdicts instead of not-assessable, making dead-holder locks detectable as stale-lock findings.
